OPERATION NOTE

Patient: PARKINSON, Albert Edward ("Bertie")   Sex: M
DOB: 03/02/1934 (aged 92)   Hosp No: WV2290457   NHS No: 485 777 3456
Address: 12 Garden Row, Martock, Somerset TA12 6LN
NOK: daughter Mrs Janet Pryce-Morgan, mob. 07700 900418
Admitted: 13.03.26 via ED   Ward: Kingfisher (orthogeriatric)
Date of operation: 14 March 2026   NCEPOD: urgent (expedited)

Surgeon: Mr Oliver Hill FRCS (Tr & Orth), Consultant
Assistant: Dr Kwame Asante-Boateng, ST4 T&O
Anaesthetist: Dr Ffion Rhys-Davies, Consultant
Scrub practitioner: SN Pauline Moss

INDICATION
92-year-old retired signalman (35 years with Great Western Railway), lives alone with carers twice daily. Tripped over the edge of a rug in his kitchen on the evening of 12/03/2026 and fell onto his right side; long lie of about 6 h until found by the morning carer. Shortened, externally rotated right leg. Radiographs: displaced intracapsular (midcervical) fracture of the right neck of femur, Garden IV.
PMH: Parkinson's disease (co-careldopa 25/100 five times daily - time-critical, doses given on time peri-op); AF on apixaban (last dose 12/3 at 18:00); CKD 3a; old right shoulder dislocation with Hill-Sachs lesion, managed non-operatively.
AMTS 7/10 on admission (baseline 9/10 per daughter). Lacks capacity for this decision: Consent Form 4 completed after best-interests meeting with daughter; Mr Parkinson himself was agreeable. Pre-op Hb 112 g/L, eGFR 52.

ANAESTHESIA
Spinal (0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine 2.4 ml) plus ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block by Dr Rhys-Davies. Light propofol sedation. ASA 3. BP pre-block 158/84. Cefuroxime 1.5 g IV and tranexamic acid 1 g IV at induction.

PROCEDURE: Right cemented hemiarthroplasty (Exeter V40 stem, unipolar head)
Left lateral, pegs, chlorhexidine prep, iodophor-impregnated drape. WHO checklist done. Knife to skin 09:42.
Modified Hardinge (direct lateral) approach. Anterior third of gluteus medius elevated in continuity with vastus lateralis. T-capsulotomy, haemarthrosis evacuated. Femoral head extracted and measured at 49 mm. Neck cut 1 cm above lesser trochanter. Box chisel, canal lateralised, broached to size 1 (offset 37.5). Trial reduction: stable, no impingement at 90 deg flexion / 30 deg internal rotation, leg lengths equal clinically.
Cement restrictor, pulsatile lavage, canal dried. Palacos R+G 2 x 40 g, retrograde gun, pressurised. Anaesthetist warned before cementing per BCIS protocol: transient BP fall to 92/50, responded to metaraminol 0.5 mg x2. Stem inserted in neutral version, head reduced.

IMPLANTS
- Exeter V40 stem 37.5 No.1, 150 mm   REF 0580-1-371   LOT 2025K0391
- Unipolar head 49 mm   LOT 77Q4019X
- Palacos R+G 40 g x2   LOT 81372644

CLOSURE
Capsule and abductors repaired transosseously with No.5 Ethibond. No.1 Vicryl to fascia lata, 2-0 Vicryl subcut, clips to skin. Levobupivacaine 0.25% 20 ml local infiltration. EBL 350 ml. Knife off 10:51.

POST-OP PLAN
1. FWB as able; no formal hip precautions (lateral approach).
2. Check AP pelvis + lateral R hip in recovery. FBC, U&E day 1.
3. Restart apixaban 2.5 mg BD at 18:00 tomorrow if no bleeding concern.
4. Parkinson's medication is time-critical - NG route if NBM.
5. Orthogeriatric review (Dr Yusuf Brennan); delirium screen (4AT) daily.
6. Clips out day 12-14 by district nurse via Martock Surgery (01935 825140).
7. Fracture clinic with Mr Hill at 6 weeks.

Signed: O. Hill, Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon, GMC 6104472   14/03/2026 11:20

Post-op diagnosis: Displaced trimalleolar fracture, right ankle - Weber B lateral malleolus, transverse medial malleolus, posterolateral (Volkmann) fragment approx. 25% of plafond on CT.
Procedure: ORIF right ankle (fibula, medial and posterior malleoli).

Clinical summary
Ms Ó Murchú is a 34-year-old secondary school teacher at Scoil Mhuire, Moate. On Saturday 11th October she was thrown from her horse while hacking out on a forestry track near Horseleap; the mare (Biscuit) shied and she landed awkwardly on her right foot. Helmet worn, GCS 15/15 throughout. Deformity reduced in ED under Entonox, below-knee backslab applied; neurovascularly intact before and after. Pain 8/10 pre-reduction, 3/10 afterwards. Plain films reported by Dr H. Weber (Consultant Radiologist); CT 12/10/26 confirmed a posterolateral fragment with some impaction. Wrinkle sign positive on the morning of surgery. Non-smoker, no diabetes. Consented by Mr Brady; infection, wound breakdown, VTE, CRPS, metalwork irritation and long-term post-traumatic arthritis discussed.

Anaesthesia
GA (LMA) with popliteal sciatic and saphenous blocks. VCV 450/5, FiO2 0.4. Transient brady to 48 bpm on tourniquet inflation, resolved with glycopyrrolate 200 mcg. Cefazolin 2 g IV pre-incision. ASA 1.

Technique and findings
Supine, sandbag under right buttock, thigh tourniquet 300 mmHg (10:05-11:31, 86 min). Lateral approach; superficial peroneal nerve protected. Short oblique Weber B fracture cleaned, reduced with pointed clamp, one 3.5 mm lag screw, then a 7-hole 1/3 tubular neutralisation plate. Posterolateral fragment reduced through the fibular window and fixed with two 4.0 mm partially threaded cannulated screws, anterior to posterior. Medial approach: periosteal flap cleared, fracture reduced, two 4.0 mm cannulated screws. Syndesmosis stressed under fluoroscopy - Cotton test and external rotation stress negative, no syndesmotic fixation. Medial clear space restored, talus congruent.
Washout, 2-0 Vicryl, 3-0 Monocryl subcuticular laterally, interrupted nylon medially. Padded backslab. EBL minimal. No complications.

Implants (traceability labels in chart)
1/3 tubular plate 7-hole    LOT 6H44120
3.5 mm cortical screws x7    LOT 7J10933
4.0 mm cannulated screws x4    LOT 2Z77815

Plan
- NWB, strict elevation, backslab 2/52 then wound check and boot.
- Tinzaparin 4,500 IU s/c daily for 6/52.
- Home when safe on crutches; sick cert for school (6 weeks initially).
- Mr Brady's fracture clinic in 2/52.
- Dr Long to send discharge summary to GP, Dr Pádraig Nolan, Main Street, Moate.

Operation: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy and primary suture repair of small umbilical hernia
Date: Friday 16 October 2026 (day-case list, Theatre 2)
Surgeon: Miss Eilidh MacLeod, Consultant Upper GI Surgeon
Assistant: Dr Lena Hartmann (CT2 Surgery)
Anaesthetist: Dr Seán Murphy (Consultant)
Scrub: Duncan Small (CN)
Post-op diagnosis: chronic calculous cholecystitis; fatty liver; umbilical hernia (defect 1.5 cm)

I operated on this pleasant 62-year-old lady today. As you know, she was admitted under our team from 02/08/2026 to 05/08/2026 with Tokyo grade I acute calculous cholecystitis (Murphy's sign positive, WCC 14.1) that settled with antibiotics. MRCP on 7 Aug showed multiple small gallstones with a normal-calibre CBD and no ductal stones. She works nights as a production supervisor at Clydeside Bakeries in Govan and was keen to have this done as a day case. Background: type 2 diabetes on metformin, BMI 34, mild asthma. ASA 2. BP on arrival 132/78.

Under GA (ETT, PCV 420/6) and with co-amoxiclav at induction, we used an open Hasson entry at the umbilicus, going through the small umbilical hernia defect, and established pneumoperitoneum at 12 mmHg. Three further 5 mm ports were placed under vision. The liver was pale and fatty with a rounded edge. The gallbladder was thick-walled and contracted with dense omental adhesions from the August episode, and Hartmann's pouch was adherent to the duodenum. Dr Hartmann took down the adhesions under my direct supervision. Rouviere's sulcus was identified and all dissection was kept above it. Calot's triangle was opened and a critical view of safety (Strasberg) was achieved and photo-documented: only two structures entering the gallbladder and the lower third of the cystic plate cleared. The cystic artery and cystic duct were each clipped (two clips staying, one on the specimen side) and divided. The gallbladder was taken off the liver bed with diathermy; there was a small breach with spillage of two stones, both retrieved, followed by a 2 litre washout. Specimen out in a retrieval bag through the umbilical port. Haemostasis checked at 8 mmHg. The umbilical fascia, including the hernia defect, was closed with interrupted 0 PDS (no mesh, defect under 2 cm). Skin 4-0 Monocryl and glue. 20 ml 0.25% bupivacaine to port sites. Swab and instrument counts correct, confirmed by CN Small. EBL under 20 ml, operating time 74 minutes. Dr Murphy gave dual PONV prophylaxis.

Histology has been sent (lab accession SK26-0114732). She can go home today once pain is 3/10 or less and she is eating and drinking; her husband Gordon is collecting her. Patient advice is also online at www.rsk-surgery.scot.nhs.uk/lapchole. No sutures to remove. I have suggested two weeks off before returning to night shifts, with no heavy lifting for 6/52 because of the hernia repair. We will phone her with the histology in about six weeks.

Yours sincerely

Miss Eilidh MacLeod
Consultant Upper GI Surgeon, GMC 7023318
